body:
## Pull request overview

Adds a new `examples/metadata-objectql` package plus accompanying ADR and guidance docs to demonstrate database-driven metadata storage patterns (CRUD, migration, hybrid loading) for view metadata via ObjectQL.

**Changes:**
- Introduces a new example workspace (`examples/metadata-objectql`) with runnable scripts and a Vitest test suite for view-metadata CRUD and migration patterns.
- Adds ADR-0002 documenting the database-driven metadata storage approach and trade-offs.
- Adds evaluation/implementation guidance docs describing recommended API + client extensions for view CRUD and batch loading.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 12 out of 12 changed files in this pull request and generated 27 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| examples/metadata-objectql/package.json | New example package scripts/deps for running examples and tests |
| examples/metadata-objectql/tsconfig.json | TS config for the example workspace |
| examples/metadata-objectql/vitest.config.ts | Vitest setup + coverage configuration for the example |
| examples/metadata-objectql/README.md | Explains goals/architecture and how to run the examples |
| examples/metadata-objectql/src/basic-example.ts | Demonstrates file-based vs in-memory metadata usage patterns |
| examples/metadata-objectql/src/view-crud.ts | Demonstrates view metadata CRUD against a DB-backed ObjectQL driver |
| examples/metadata-objectql/src/migration-example.ts | Demonstrates filesystem → DB migration + hybrid fallback loader |
| examples/metadata-objectql/test/metadata-service.test.ts | Adds CRUD/query/pagination/edge-case tests for the example |
| docs/adr/0002-database-driven-metadata-storage.md | ADR documenting the database-driven metadata storage pattern |
| docs/METADATA_SERVICE_EVALUATION.md | Assessment of API/client/doc gaps and recommendations |
| docs/METADATA_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md | Summary of delivered examples/docs/tests |
| docs/METADATA_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md | Step-by-step guidance for adding endpoints + client methods |
</details>
The query options use `filters`/`offset`, but the DataEngine protocol uses `filter` and `skip` for pagination. Using the wrong keys will cause the conditions/pagination to be ignored by ObjectQL.

This package is `"type": "module"`, so `require`/`require.main` is not defined in Node ESM. The direct-run guard will crash when executed via `tsx`. Use an ESM-safe entry check (e.g., comparing `import.meta.url`) or remove the guard and rely on the package scripts to run the file explicitly.

The API paths in this document use `/api/v1/metadata/...`, but the repo’s discovery/routes conventions use the metadata prefix `/api/v1/meta` (see `ApiRoutesSchema.metadata` in `packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts`). To avoid sending readers to non-existent endpoints, update the examples to the correct route prefix and path structure (e.g., `/api/v1/meta/...`).

`setDefaultDriver('memory')` isn’t part of the ObjectQL engine API, and the InMemoryDriver’s driver name is `com.objectstack.driver.memory` (not `memory`). Set the default by calling `registerDriver(driver, true)` (or rely on first-driver default) and remove `setDefaultDriver`.
```suggestion
  objectql.registerDriver(driver, true);
```

`HybridMetadataService.load()` is using `filters` (plural) in the query options. ObjectQL’s DataEngine contract uses `filter` (singular); with the current engine this condition will be ignored and can return incorrect results.

This example package is ESM (`type: module`), so `require.main === module` will throw at runtime when run via `tsx`. Use an ESM-safe entrypoint check (via `import.meta.url`) or remove the guard and rely on the pnpm scripts to run the file.

The InMemoryDriver/ObjectQL insert path returns records with an `id` field (not `_id`). These assertions will fail as written; update the test to assert on `id` (and pass `id` through subsequent update/delete calls).

In the proposed Zod API schemas/snippets, fields like `object_name` and `is_default` are snake_case. In `@objectstack/spec`, schema property keys are consistently camelCase (e.g., `routes.metadata`, `features.websockets`). Consider changing these to `objectName` / `isDefault` (and keep snake_case only for machine *values*, not JSON property keys) to match spec conventions and prevent client confusion.

The guide’s route examples use `/api/v1/metadata/...`, but the platform’s configured metadata base route is `/api/v1/meta` (per discovery / dispatcher defaults). If these snippets are intended to be copy-pasteable, update the route prefixes (and any client URLs) to match `/api/v1/meta/...` so implementations don’t end up with mismatched discovery vs actual routes.

`ObjectQL.delete()` does not take `(object, id)`. The engine expects delete options (e.g., `filter`) and will throw if no id can be extracted. Update this to pass the id via `options.filter` or include `id`/`_id` in the data according to the current DataEngine delete contract.
```suggestion
    await objectql.delete('sys_view', { filter: { _id: existing._id } });
```

`objectql.registerObject(SysMetadata)` isn’t part of the current ObjectQL engine API. Register the `sys_metadata` schema through the registry (`objectql.registry` / `SchemaRegistry`) using the supported registration method so subsequent `find/insert/update` calls can resolve the object schema correctly.
```suggestion
  objectql.registry.register(SysMetadata);
```

This file is executed in an ESM package (`type: module`), but it uses `require('crypto')`. That will throw at runtime. Switch to `import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'` (or equivalent ESM import) and avoid `require` usage here.

The ObjectQL query/update calls here use non-standard options (`filters`) and an `(object, id, data)` update signature. Current ObjectQL expects query options like `filter` (not `filters`) and `update(object, data, options?)` (id extracted from `data.id`/`data._id` or `options.filter`). As written, lookups/updates will be ignored or throw at runtime—please align these calls with the DataEngine contract.

`ObjectQL.update()` does not support the `(object, id, patch)` signature used here. The engine signature is `update(object, data, options?)` and extracts the id from `data.id`/`data._id` or `options.filter`. Update this test to use the supported update contract (and the correct id field).

The query options use `filters` (plural), but the DataEngine contract uses `filter` (singular). With the current engine, these conditions will be ignored and the tests may pass/fail nondeterministically depending on inserted data.

`ObjectQL.delete()` expects delete options (e.g., `filter`) and will throw if no id can be extracted. Passing a raw id string as the second argument won’t delete anything with the current engine API—update the test to call delete using the supported DataEngine delete contract (and use `id`, not `_id`).

The query option key should be `filter` (per DataEngineQueryOptions), not `filters`. As written, `findOne` will ignore the conditions and can return unexpected rows (or always null depending on driver). Update the examples to use `filter` with the supported filter shape.
```suggestion
      filter: { name: viewName }
```

This package is `type: module`, so `require.main === module` is not valid in ESM and will crash when running the script via `tsx`. Use an ESM-compatible main-module check (based on `import.meta.url`) or remove the guard.

`setDefaultDriver('memory')` isn’t part of the current ObjectQL engine API, and the InMemoryDriver’s name is `com.objectstack.driver.memory` (not `memory`). Set the default by calling `registerDriver(driver, true)` (or rely on first-driver default) and remove `setDefaultDriver`.
```suggestion
    objectql.registerDriver(driver, true);
```

The architecture diagram labels the persisted store as “View Metadata (In Memory)”, but this example’s stated goal is database-driven metadata. Consider updating the diagram/labels to reflect database persistence (and optionally show the registry cache as a separate in-memory layer) to avoid confusion for readers.
```suggestion
│   (Database)    │      │  (Postgres/SQL)  │
```

This summary claims “Code review passed” / “Tests passing” and has a placeholder PR number (`#[TBD]`). Since this file lands in-repo, those statements will quickly become stale/misleading. Recommend removing the “passed” assertions or rephrasing to neutral language (and avoid hardcoding a PR number placeholder).

`validatedView` is computed but never used, and the record stores the original `viewDefinition`. If the schema strips unknown keys/coerces values, you’ll persist unvalidated data. Persist the parsed output (e.g., the validated `list` value) to ensure the stored JSON matches the spec.
```suggestion
  const { list: validatedListView } = ViewSchema.parse({ list: viewDefinition });
  
  // Prepare the metadata record using the validated definition
  const viewRecord = {
    name: viewName,
    object_name: objectName,
    label: validatedListView.label || viewName,
    type: validatedListView.type || 'grid',
    definition: validatedListView, // Store schema-validated definition as JSON
```
